name: DELPHI functional-scoring compensation rule base
purpose: Decide, BY RULE and from cited evidence, whether a documented compensation mechanism can be invoked for a gene that is absent or broken in a designed organism. The default is refusal: a gap is only ever COMPENSATORY when a rule fires and names its source.

design_stance.burden_of_proof: on the compensation claim, never on the gap
design_stance.never: return a class asserting compensation without a rule_id and at least one source with a locator
design_stance.critical_separation: A documented compensation mechanism is evidence that an ADAPTING GENE IS UPREGULATED. It is NOT evidence that the FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENT IS MET. See rule TA-NOT-FUNCTIONAL-RESCUE (R07) and the vegfaa case.

classes.documented: This gene, in this organism, has a published compensation outcome. The verdict is read off the case table, not inferred.
classes.plausible-by-rule: No published outcome for this gene, but every condition of a rule derived from primary evidence is satisfied. Weaker than 'documented' and must never be scored as equal to it.
classes.not-expected: A rule positively excludes compensation (not merely 'no evidence found'). Confident refusal.
classes.unknown: The inputs a rule needs are absent. Explicitly NOT a licence to assume compensation, and explicitly NOT evidence against it.

mechanism_kinds.transcriptional-adaptation: Mutant-mRNA-decay-triggered, sequence-similarity-dependent upregulation of an adapting gene. Requires mRNA to be made AND degraded. Absent from knockdowns.
mechanism_kinds.protein-feedback: The lost protein normally represses a relative; losing it de-represses that relative. Mechanistically independent of mRNA decay, and therefore ALSO seen in knockdowns.
mechanism_kinds.paralogue-buffering: A paralogue already expressed in the right place and time carries the function, with no induced change required.

allele_kinds.comment: Maps a design lesion onto the mRNA fate that the mechanism requires. 'mrna_made' and 'mrna_decayed' are what the rules actually test.

frameshift.note: introduces a downstream PTC; NMD substrate unless the PTC falls in the last exon
frameshift.WARNING: A frameshift allele is NOT reliably a decay-triggering allele. Frameshift indels introduced by genome editing can cause skipping of the affected in-frame exon, and the resulting transcript escapes NMD entirely (lalonde2017, cited by stainier2017guidelines ref 9 and by falcucci2025). The classifier cannot detect this, so 'frameshift' carries a confidence penalty relative to a confirmed PTC with measured mRNA decay.

splice-essential.note: usually produces an NMD substrate; confidence lower than a direct PTC

last-exon-deletion.note: explicitly among the allele classes El-Brolosy 2019 analysed as showing transcriptional adaptation

start-loss.note: mRNA is made but not translated; PTC recognition is translation-dependent, so it is not expected to be an NMD substrate. Mechanism-inferred, not directly tested.

gene-absent.note: THE COMMON CASE for a designed organism: the design simply does not carry the gene. Behaves as an RNA-less allele.

knockdown-morpholino.note: target mRNA is present and blocked, not degraded

rnai.note: mRNA IS degraded, but by the RNAi route; transcriptional adaptation was not demonstrated for RNAi in the sourced zebrafish work. Treated as knockdown, i.e. refused, and flagged as a known gap.

crispri.note: obstructs transcription, so no mutant mRNA is made to decay; Rossi 2015 and El-Brolosy 2026 both use it as the negative control

various-null.note: An AGGREGATE over several alleles of a gene whose individual lesion classes are not resolved (how ZFIN records a gene). Both mRNA fates are null, so such a row can never match a specific allele kind in the case lookup -- by design. These rows are corroborating context (a null had a severe phenotype), NOT evidence that compensation was tested and absent.

author_correction.citation: Author Correction: PTC-bearing mRNA elicits a genetic compensation response via Upf3a and COMPASS components. Nature 654(8120):E32 (2026), published online 9 June 2026.
author_correction.content: RETRIEVED AND IT IS TRIVIAL. The correction fixes one y-axis tick label in one extended-data panel. No data, figure panel or conclusion was altered or retracted.
author_correction.quote: In the version of this article initially published, there was a labeling mistake on the y-axis of Extended Data Fig. 1l ("Area (pixel) at 3.5 dpf"): the original values ranging from 1,000 to 2000 should have read 1,000 to 1,500.
author_correction.quote2: Due to the age of the article, the figure cannot be updated directly. A revised Extended Data Fig. 1 is available as Supplementary Information alongside this amendment. This notice serves to correct the article.
author_correction.CORRECTION_TO_THIS_FILE: An earlier draft of this rule base capped confidence on ma2019 because the correction's content was unknown. That cap was UNJUSTIFIED and has been removed. The correction gives no reason to discount the Upf3a/COMPASS mechanism.

ma2019.caveat: Still abstract-only for the text itself (not open access, not in Europe PMC full text), so no figure-level locators are given for ma2019 quotes. The real counter-evidence to its mechanism is Mellis 2024, which found no correlation between COMPASS component expression and paralogue upregulation -- see rule R02 counter-evidence.

elbrolosy2017rev.access: Open access; FULL TEXT read. This is a REVIEW: it is used only for mechanism taxonomy and for pointers to primary cases, never as primary evidence for a number.

welker2023.citation: Welker JM, Rossi A, Stainier DYR et al. Partial sequence identity in a 25-nucleotide long element is sufficient for transcriptional adaptation in the Caenorhabditis elegans act-5/act-3 model. PLoS Genet 19(6):e1010806 (2023).
welker2023.caveat: SPECIES TRANSFER. This is the only source that localises the required similarity to a short defined element, and it is a nematode, not a fish. Any rule leaning on it is marked species_transfer: true and capped at 'medium' confidence.

xie2025.citation: Xie L, Jakutis G, Dooley CM, Guenther S, Kontarakis Z, Howard SP, Juan T, Stainier DYR. Induction of a transcriptional adaptation response by RNA destabilization events. EMBO Rep (2025).
xie2025.access: Open access; abstract and introduction read in full.

Mechanisms linking cytoplasmic decay of translation-defective mRNA to transcriptional adaptation. Science (2026).
elbrolosy2026.access: Open access author manuscript; FULL TEXT read.

stainier2017guidelines.importance: A 24-author community guideline that lists genetic compensation as ONE OF FOUR explanations for the morphant/mutant gap, not the default. The single most useful source for keeping this rule base honest.

ttn2_2026.citation: Truncating titin (ttn.2) variants in zebrafish. Circulation Research (2026).
ttn2_2026.access: Open access; read by a delegated sweep, quotes verbatim-verified against the cached XML.
ttn2_2026.importance: THE decisive case for R07: paralogue upregulated at TRANSCRIPT AND PROTEIN level (2.55-fold Ttn.1 peptides) and the phenotype was still not rescued.

fbn3_2026.citation: Fibrillin-3 (fbn3) truncating allele in zebrafish. JACC Basic to Translational Science (2026).
fbn3_2026.access: Open access; read by a delegated sweep.
fbn3_2026.importance: Compensation tested and absent: fbn1 and fbn2 were NOT upregulated. Also a clean example of transcriptional adaptation absent while functional redundancy is present.

pomgnt2_2026.citation: Impact of maternal compensation on developmental phenotypes in a zebrafish model of severe congenital muscular dystrophy. PLoS Genet (2026).
pomgnt2_2026.access: Open access; read by a delegated sweep.
pomgnt2_2026.importance: The maternal-rescue confound, with compensation tested and absent, AND an explicit statement from the journal's editors that maternal rescue is not genetic compensation.

marszalek2026yeast.citation: Marszalek M, Babik W, Korona R, Tomala K. Signatures of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay but no evidence for transcriptional adaptation associated with protein-truncating variants in wild yeast diploids. Mol Biol Evol 43(9):msag219 (2026).
marszalek2026yeast.importance: The main published absence-of-signal result. A taxon boundary condition, NOT a refutation of the zebrafish work.

lalonde2017.citation: Lalonde S, et al. Frameshift indels introduced by genome editing can lead to in-frame exon skipping. PLoS ONE (2017).
lalonde2017.access: NOT READ. Reached this rule base as reference 9 of stainier2017guidelines and via falcucci2025. Cited only for the caveat it supports.

falcucci2025.citation: Falcucci L, et al. Transcriptional adaptation upregulates utrophin in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Nature 639:493-502 (2025).
falcucci2025.access: Open access; read by a delegated sweep.
falcucci2025.caveat: Measures transcript, pre-mRNA and protein but NEVER tests phenotype rescue; all cell culture. Its functional claim is imported from mouse genetics.

nphp_2022.citation: Nephrocystin (nphp1/nphp4/nphp8) mutant zebrafish. Human Molecular Genetics (2022).
nphp_2022.access: Open access; read by a delegated sweep.
nphp_2022.importance: The counter-direction on the maternal confound: removing the maternal contribution made phenotypes milder, not worse.

howe2013.access: Full text retrieved via NCBI efetch (Europe PMC fullTextXML returns HTTP 500 for this PMCID).

kettleborough2013.importance: The largest systematic zebrafish knockout phenotype screen, and it argues AGAINST paralogue redundancy as the explanation for silent nulls.

mellis2024.citation: Mellis IA, Melzer ME, Bodkin N, Goyal Y. Prevalence of and gene regulatory constraints on transcriptional adaptation in single cells. Genome Biology 25:217 (2024).
mellis2024.organism: human and mouse (bulk RNA-seq and Perturb-seq)
mellis2024.importance: Best available genome-scale answer to 'how often does paralogue upregulation follow a knockout': 16/74.

bailonzambrano2022.citation: Bailon-Zambrano R, Sucharov J, Mumme-Monheit A, Murry M, Stenzel A, Pulvino AT, Mitchell JM, Colborn KL, Nichols JT. Variable paralog expression underlies phenotype variation. eLife 11:e79247 (2022).
bailonzambrano2022.importance: THE key source for R06: buffering strength tracks paralogue EXPRESSION LEVEL, in zebrafish, and the buffering paralogue has no phenotype of its own.

chrystal2026.citation: Chrystal PW et al. Two zebrafish pcdh15 paralogs cooperate in sensory organ development. Communications Biology 9:1048 (2026).
chrystal2026.importance: Same paralogue pair buffers in one tissue and not in another -- direct evidence that buffering is tissue-specific.

ross2022.citation: Ross JA, Ren H, Zhang Y, Chi NC, Hamilton MK. Mutation of zebrafish Ankfn1 and Ankfn1-like paralogs. G3 12(3):jkab446 (2022).
ross2022.importance: Quantified buffering by genotype class and showed it is ASYMMETRIC between the ancestral and derived copy.

obrien2026.citation: O'Brien S, Fujimoto MH, Lowe AR, Berger AH. Transcriptional adaptation influences buffering among essential paralog gene families. Preprint (2026).
obrien2026.access: PREPRINT, ABSTRACT ONLY. Not open access in Europe PMC; bioRxiv returned HTTP 429 then Cloudflare 1015 on every attempt. NOT peer reviewed.
obrien2026.caveat: Used for one rate only, clearly flagged as unverified.

zfin_omics.citation: ZFIN phenotype and Ensembl Compara paralogue rows as integrated in this repo at omics/genomic/annotations.jsonl.gz (ZFIN release 2026-10-31, Ensembl release 116 / GRCz11).
zfin_omics.access: Local. 87,041 allele_phenotype rows (54,452 reagent='allele', 32,589 reagent='knockdown/crispant'); 2,263 paralog rows; 2,742 paralog_count rows.
zfin_omics.caveat: ZFIN allele_phenotype rows are NOT a clean readout of 'this mutant has a phenotype'. Many rows for phenotypically wild-type genes are bookkeeping annotations such as 'whole organism increased amount' / 'decreased amount' / 'absent', which record Mendelian ratios and lethality rather than a morphological defect. Row counts are used here only as corroboration, never to decide a compensation verdict.

rules.name: An allele that makes no mRNA cannot trigger transcriptional adaptation
rules.why: Transcriptional adaptation is triggered by the decay of the mutant transcript. If the lesion removes the promoter or the whole locus, or blocks transcription, there is no transcript to decay, so the trigger does not exist. This was tested directly by building RNA-less alleles.
rules.delphi_note: THIS IS THE RULE THAT FIRES MOST OFTEN FOR A DESIGNED ORGANISM. When a design simply does not carry the required gene, that is an RNA-less state, and transcriptional adaptation is positively excluded, not merely unevidenced.

sources.quote: Alleles that fail to transcribe the mutated gene do not exhibit transcriptional adaptation, and these alleles give rise to more severe phenotypes than alleles displaying mutant mRNA decay.

sources.locator: Results, 'Sequence similarity and transcriptional adaptation' preceding paragraph; Fig. 3a
sources.quote: Indeed, RNA-less alleles of hbegfa, vegfaa and alcama fail to upregulate hbegfb, vegfab and alcamb, respectively (Fig. 3a).
Therefore, use of RNA-less alleles can uncover phenotypes not observed in alleles exhibiting mutant mRNA degradation.
Moreover, egfl7 CRISPR interference, which obstructs transcript elongation and causes severe vascular defects, does not cause the upregulation of these genes.
By contrast, CRISPR-interference (CRISPRi) would repress transcription without inducing mRNA decay, and thereby fail to induce TA.

counter_evidence.note: El-Brolosy 2019 found the egfl7 RNA-less allele still showed SOME emilin upregulation, only milder. So 'no mRNA' abolishes the adaptation response incompletely in at least one case, rather than to zero.
counter_evidence.quote: the mutants displayed pronounced vascular defects (Fig. 3f) as well as milder upregulation of the emilin genes

counter_evidence.note: This rule excludes TRANSCRIPTIONAL ADAPTATION only. A paralogue that is constitutively expressed in the right tissue and stage can still buffer an RNA-less or absent gene without any induced change. That path is R06, not this rule.

rules.name: Transcriptional adaptation requires a lesion that destabilises the mutant mRNA
rules.consequence: permits 'plausible-by-rule' IF R05 and R06 also pass
rules.why: The trigger is the destabilisation of the mutant transcript, shown three ways: blocking NMD (upf1 loss, pharmacological NMD inhibition, translation block) abolishes the response; inducing decay artificially with uncapped RNA creates the response in wild types; and protecting the same RNA from exonuclease decay abolishes it again.

sources.quote: Inactivating upf1 in these mutants led to decreased levels of mutant mRNA decay (Extended Data Fig. 5a) and loss of transcriptional adaptation (Fig. 2a).
injection of uncapped hif1ab or vegfaa RNAs with an upstream sequence which renders them resistant to 5' to 3' exonuclease-mediated decay did not induce transcriptional adaptation

sources.locator: Results, first paragraph; Extended Data Fig. 1
sources.quote: We started by analyzing different zebrafish and mouse mutants that harbor a premature termination codon (PTC) or have their last exon deleted
we show that mRNA bearing a premature termination codon (PTC) promptly triggers a GCR that involves Upf3a and components of the COMPASS complex.
Together, these data highlight the critical role of RNA destabilization events as a trigger for TA, or at least a TA-like response.

counter_evidence.note: The requirement is DESTABILISATION, not a PTC as such. Xie 2025 obtained the same adapting-gene upregulation with Cas13d mRNA cleavage and with ribozyme pre-mRNA cleavage, neither of which involves a PTC. So any lesion that destabilises the transcript qualifies, and conversely a PTC is not magic.
counter_evidence.quote: We find that both types of perturbations are effective in degrading Actg1 mRNA, and that they both upregulate Actg2.

counter_evidence.note: A PTC in the LAST exon typically escapes NMD, so 'nonsense' is not uniformly a decay trigger. Position within the transcript is not modelled here; this is a known gap.

DECISIVE LIMIT ON THIS RULE. A PTC is NOT sufficient. In the very same genes, El-Brolosy found two other PTC-bearing alleles that show no transcriptional adaptation at all, while the lab's own alleles do. So allele identity, not lesion class, determines the outcome -- and our classifier only ever sees a lesion class. This is the single biggest reason 'plausible-by-rule' must never be scored as equal to 'documented'.
counter_evidence.quote: while analyzing various mutant alleles, we found that unlike hbegfaΔ7 and vclaΔ13, two other PTC bearing alleles, hbegfasa18135 and vclasa14599, do not display transcriptional adaptation

counter_evidence.note: Transcriptional adaptation is dose-sensitive and dominant: heterozygotes show a weaker response. A design carrying one broken copy is therefore not equivalent to a homozygous null.
counter_evidence.locator: Results, first paragraph; Extended Data Fig. 2b
counter_evidence.quote: we found that vcla, hif1ab and egfl7 heterozygous animals also display transcriptional adaptation, albeit less pronounced than that observed in the homozygous mutants

counter_evidence.note: PARTIAL REPLICATION FAILURE. An independent group re-analysed El-Brolosy's own three mouse models and could only confirm one of the three as significant under their bootstrap pipeline.
counter_evidence.quote: while we observed some degree of transcriptional upregulation in paralogs of all 3 target genes, only Actb was deemed significant by our bootstrap analysis pipeline.

counter_evidence.note: THE Ma 2019 MECHANISM DID NOT REPLICATE AS A PREDICTOR. The same independent group found no relationship between COMPASS component levels and whether a knockout showed paralogue upregulation. The mechanism may be real without being usable as a predictive feature.
counter_evidence.quote: we did not observe correlation between expression levels of proposed mediators of transcriptional adaptation (e.g., COMPASS complex components) and whether a CRISPR target demonstrated paralog upregulation.

counter_evidence.note: TAXON BOUNDARY. A population-genomic survey of 2,863 protein-truncating variants across 598 genes and 282 wild yeast strains found clear NMD signatures and no transcriptional adaptation signature. The authors attribute this to yeast lacking the metazoan machinery, so this bounds the taxon range rather than refuting the fish result -- but it means transcriptional adaptation is not a property of eukaryotes in general.
counter_evidence.quote: However, despite evidence of this mRNA surveillance activity, we did not detect a clear signature of transcriptional adaptation.
counter_evidence.quote2: Overall, our findings suggest that TA is not a universal response to loss-of-function mutations in yeast.

counter_evidence.note: Where the yeast study did find allele-specific upregulation, the effect was 2.7%, and no variant showed both significant NMD and 2-fold upregulation.
counter_evidence.locator: Results, 'Rare cases of allele-specific up-regulation'; Fig. 6c
counter_evidence.quote: Although statistically significant, the estimated increase was small (2.7%).
counter_evidence.quote2: Within this PTV subset, no cases exhibited both significant NMD and at least a 2-fold upregulation, whereas only 8 such cases were identified across all PTVs.

rules.name: A missense, in-frame or synonymous allele must NOT be classed compensable
rules.basis: mechanism-inferred from directly tested premises. FLAGGED: the decisive experiment (a missense allele of a gene with documented transcriptional adaptation, shown to fail to adapt) was NOT found in the sources read.
rules.why: A missense transcript is translated normally and is not an NMD substrate, so it is not destabilised; by R02 the trigger is destabilisation; therefore no transcriptional adaptation is expected. Ma et al. make the same inference explicit in reverse when they propose CREATING a PTC as a way to bring missense alleles under the compensation response.

sources.quote: may help lead to the development of therapeutic strategies that treat missense mutations associated with genetic disorders by either creating a PTC in the mutated gene or introducing a transgene containing a PTC to trigger a GCR.
we demonstrate that the GCR is dependent on both the presence of a PTC and the nucleotide sequence of the transgene mRNA, which is homologous to the compensatory endogenous genes.
by analysing several models of transcriptional adaptation in zebrafish and mouse, we uncover a requirement for mutant mRNA degradation.

counter_evidence.note: IMPORTANT EXCEPTION. Because the real requirement is destabilisation (R02 counter-evidence), a missense allele whose transcript happens to be destabilised for some other reason -- a disrupted splice signal, a created destabilising element, altered secondary structure -- could in principle trigger adaptation. The classifier therefore downgrades this rule to 'unknown' whenever the caller explicitly reports that the missense transcript is destabilised (input mrnaDestabilised: true).

'start-loss' is the weakest member of this group. The claim that PTC recognition is translation-dependent rests on El-Brolosy's use of a translation block as an NMD-inhibition proxy in mouse Rela K.O. cells, not on a start-loss allele.

A missense allele may be compensated by a mechanism OTHER than transcriptional adaptation -- notably a protein feedback loop (R08) or constitutive paralogue buffering (R06). This rule refuses transcriptional adaptation only, and the classifier still consults those paths.

SUPPORTING HUMAN DATA POINT, indirect. Patients with in-frame DMD deletions have been reported not to show utrophin upregulation, while the decay-competent alleles do. Reached this rule base through falcucci2025's introduction; the primary source (Anthony et al., JAMA Neurol 2014;71:32-40) was NOT read.
counter_evidence.quote: By contrast, patients with in-frame deletions in DMD have been reported not to show utrophin upregulation

counter_evidence.note: The therapeutic framing of the field confirms the rule's direction and its inferential status: missense alleles are treated as needing decay ENGINEERED IN, because they do not trigger adaptation by themselves.
counter_evidence.quote: This method could be used in patients with missense mutations as well as in those with frameshift or nonsense mutations as increased RNA degradation can further upregulate compensating genes

counter_evidence.note: El-Brolosy et al. themselves present the missense/in-frame prediction as an untested HYPOTHESIS, not a result. Their wording is 'we propose' and 'will help test this hypothesis'. R03's confidence reflects that.
counter_evidence.quote: we propose that nonsense mutations might be less common as they might lead to mRNA decay-triggered upregulation of related genes and therefore not cause significant symptoms. Detailed transcriptomic analyses of relevant individuals will help test this hypothesis.

rules.name: Knockdown does not trigger transcriptional adaptation -- which is why morphants and mutants differ
rules.basis: literature-derived, directly tested; this is the founding observation of the field
rules.why: A morpholino blocks translation or splicing of a transcript that is still present and not degraded; CRISPRi stops the transcript being made at all. Neither produces the decay products that trigger adaptation. The resulting phenotype gap between knockdown and mutant is large and systematic.
rules.scoring_consequence: If a DELPHI design reduces a gene's dose rather than nulling it, the compensation class is refused. A knockdown-like design gap does not get to borrow the mutant literature.

sources.quote: Genetic compensation induced by deleterious mutations but not gene knockdowns.
Taken together, these data reveal the activation of a compensatory network to buffer against deleterious mutations, which was not observed after translational or transcriptional knockdown.
Similarly, vegfaa mutants but not morphants show an upregulation of vegfab.
egfl7 mutants do not show any obvious phenotypes while animals injected with egfl7 morpholino (morphants) exhibit severe vascular defects.
Unlike capn3a-knockdown embryos, which have small livers, and nid1a-knockdown embryos, which have short body lengths, capn3a-null and nid1a-null mutants appear normal.

a comparison of published morphant defects with the Sanger Zebrafish Mutation Project revealed that approximately 80% of morphant phenotypes were not observed in mutant embryos, similar to our mutant collection.

counter_evidence.note: MAJOR AND UNRESOLVED. Kok et al. read the same morphant/mutant discrepancy as evidence that MORPHOLINOS ARE UNRELIABLE, not that mutants are compensated, and they report that they could not attribute the missing mutant phenotypes to maternal effects or incomplete loss of function. Under their reading the ~80% figure says nothing about compensation at all. Both readings are live in the literature; this rule base uses the discrepancy only to refuse compensation for knockdowns, which is the direction both readings support.
counter_evidence.quote: The absence of phenotypes in mutant embryos was not likely due to maternal effects or failure to eliminate gene function.

counter_evidence.note: RNAi is classed as knockdown here, yet RNAi DOES degrade the target mRNA, so by R02's logic it might trigger adaptation. No source read here tested RNAi for transcriptional adaptation in zebrafish. Classing it as a refusal is the CONSERVATIVE choice and is flagged as an unsourced decision, not a finding.

THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT IN THIS WHOLE RULE BASE. A 24-author community guideline, with Stainier as first author, lists genetic compensation as ONE OF FOUR candidate explanations for the morphant/mutant gap -- alongside maternal rescue, morpholino off-target effects, and the mutant allele being hypomorphic rather than null. The field's own consensus document does not treat compensation as the default explanation, and neither may this rule base.
counter_evidence.locator: body text, 'This brief document provides an updated set of guidelines'
counter_evidence.quote: MO-induced phenotypes are often more severe than those of the corresponding mutants, which could be due to the following:
the_four: phenotypic rescue of zygotic mutants by maternally provided wild-type mRNAs
off-target effects of the MO (e.g., Kok et al. 2015)
the hypomorphic nature of the mutant allele analyzed
genetic compensation in mutant but not MO-injected animals (e.g., Rossi et al. 2015)

counter_evidence.note: Morpholino off-target toxicity is substantial and partly p53-mediated, which is an alternative explanation for morphant severity that has nothing to do with compensation. Note particularly that off-targeting is indistinguishable between maternal and zygotic transcripts, so it cannot be ruled out by timing.
counter_evidence.locator: guidelines body, citing Robu et al. 2007 PLoS Genet 3(5):e78 (PMID 17530925)
counter_evidence.quote: About 15-20% of MOs used in zebrafish show off-targeting effects
counter_evidence.note2: The Robu figure was read by a delegated sweep from the cached PMC1877875 XML, not by me directly.

counter_evidence.note: Demonstrating that a zebrafish allele is a true null is itself hard, which undercuts the premise of every mutant-versus-morphant comparison in this rule base.
counter_evidence.quote: demonstrating that an allele is a null can be challenging either genetically, as very few deficiency alleles are available in zebrafish, or biochemically

counter_evidence.note: Protein-feedback compensation is NOT excluded by this rule and is in fact detectable in knockdowns -- that is the discriminator in R08.
counter_evidence.locator: section 'Upregulation of related genes following a gene knockout', paragraph 1
counter_evidence.quote: Upregulation of related genes due to the loss of a negative feedback loop may be the first hypothesis to test when a mutant fails to show a phenotype, and a knockdown approach may help test it.

rules.name: The compensating gene must share sequence similarity with the mutant mRNA
rules.consequence: necessary condition for 'plausible-by-rule'; its absence forces 'not-expected', its unknown-ness forces 'unknown'
rules.confidence: high for 'similarity is required'; medium for the location detail

where_must_the_similarity_lie.answer: NOT the whole transcript. Similarity located in the adapting gene's EXONS or INTRONS induces adaptation; similarity in its 3'UTR does NOT; similarity in its promoter gives only a mild response. On the mutant-mRNA side, the one mapped element lies between the PTC and the next exon/exon junction. A 25 bp element at 60% identity was sufficient in the one model where this was mapped.
where_must_the_similarity_lie.evidence_grade: the exon/intron-vs-3'UTR result is from a single zebrafish model (hif1ab/epas1a); the 25 bp element is from a single C. elegans model (act-5/act-3)

operational_definition_used_by_the_sourc.similar_gene: a partial BLASTn match anywhere inside the target gene body or within 2 kb upstream of its TSS
operational_definition_used_by_the_sourc.blast_settings: BLASTn word size 7, E-value up to 1,000,000
operational_definition_used_by_the_sourc.WARNING: That E-value threshold is extraordinarily permissive. Almost any pair of genes will have SOME match at E=1e6. This rule therefore must NOT be implemented as 'ran BLAST, got a hit'. The classifier requires either (a) a named published adapting-gene relationship, or (b) a paralogue relationship with a stated percent identity, and it records the identity figure so a reader can judge it.

sources.locator: Results, 'Sequence similarity and transcriptional adaptation'; Extended Data Fig. 8g

rules.name: A paralogue can only buffer if it is actually expressed in the required tissue and stage
rules.consequence: permits 'plausible-by-rule'. If expression evidence is ABSENT -> 'unknown'. If the omics layer asserts not_expressed_in for the required anatomy -> 'not-expected'.
rules.basis: literature-derived, in zebrafish, by two independent routes: buffering strength tracks paralogue expression LEVEL (Bailon-Zambrano 2022), and buffering is TISSUE-SPECIFIC for a single paralogue pair (Chrystal 2026). The remaining guard element is only that no source has validated this as a predictive rule across many genes.
rules.why: Paralogue EXISTENCE is close to uninformative in zebrafish: 26% of zebrafish genes sit in ohnologue pairs from the teleost genome duplication, while compensation is uncommon. The only version of this condition that discriminates asks whether the paralogue is expressed where and when the function is required. Two zebrafish studies make that the causal variable rather than a plausible one: in mef2ca, heritable variation in paralogue expression level is what varies buffering across wild-type populations; in pcdh15a/b, the same pair buffers in retina and not in the mechanosensory lineage. Our transcriptomic omics layer supplies exactly the needed inputs: expressed_in with anatomy and stages, not_expressed_in, and expression_level in TPM.

omics_link.paralogue_source: omics/genomic feature 'paralog' (Ensembl Compara release 116, within_species_paralog, carries identity_pct)

sources.note: Why existence is uninformative: ohnologue pairs are ordinary. The authors exclude intrachromosomal pairs, so 26% is a floor.

counter_evidence.note: DECISIVE NEGATIVE EVIDENCE AGAINST PARALOGUE OPTIMISM. In the largest systematic survey read, 1 of 439 possible paralogous pairs met the strict criteria, and even a deliberately over-permissive criterion reached only 156 of 439 (35.5%), of which the authors say most are unlikely to be real. Paralogue existence therefore predicts buffering very poorly, and this rule must never be allowed to fire on existence alone.

Our paralogue data is ASYMMETRIC. Ensembl Compara rows in omics/genomic do not always appear on both members of a pair: vclb lists vcla as a paralogue at 85.7% identity, but vcla carries no paralog row; alcamb lists alcama, alcama carries none. The classifier must therefore accept paralogues passed in by the caller and must not read 'no paralog row' as 'no paralogue'. It returns 'unknown' in that situation, not 'not-expected'.
An expressed paralogue is still not a functional equivalent. Subfunctionalisation after the teleost duplication is the norm, so co-expression is necessary but nowhere near sufficient.

THE LARGEST SYSTEMATIC ZEBRAFISH SCREEN EXPLICITLY REJECTS PARALOGUE REDUNDANCY as the main explanation for silent nulls, and offers two competing explanations ahead of it (partially-disrupting point mutations, and a phenotyping window limited to morphology and behaviour in the first 5 dpf). This is the strongest single argument against letting R06 carry much weight.
counter_evidence.quote: Finally, the teleost-specific genome duplication might cause paralogue redundancy. While this is possible there are few examples of paralogues being completely redundant. In contrast, there are numerous paralogue pairs where gene expression domains and functions have split between paralogues.

counter_evidence.note: Buffering is ASYMMETRIC between the ancestral and derived copy of a pair: losing the derived Ankfn1 copy gave 7% penetrance, losing the ancestral copy gave 0/110. Our paralogue input carries no ancestral/derived annotation, so the classifier cannot express this and will treat the two directions alike. Known gap.
counter_evidence.quote: Inactivation of the Chr12 (derived) paralog alone was sufficient for weak penetrance of the larval and swim bladder phenotypes (7% of offspring), while inactivation of the Chr24 (ancestral) paralog had no detected effect on these phenotypes (0/110).

counter_evidence.note: Demonstrated paralogue buffering is RARE in the literature, not a background assumption.
counter_evidence.quote: Few examples of paralogous gene pairs in zebrafish for which disruption of both copies creates a phenotype that differs from knockout of either paralog alone have been published

scope_limit.applies_to: null-like alleles only (mrna_made false, or mrna_decayed true)
scope_limit.why: Every sourced paralogue-buffering case in this base -- mef2ca (bailonzambrano2022), pcdh15a/b (chrystal2026), ankfn1 (ross2022) -- uses a loss-of-function allele. There is NO sourced case of a paralogue buffering a missense allele. A missense product can also be dominant-negative, which a paralogue cannot buffer at all.
scope_limit.provenance: ADDED AFTER A FAILING TEST. The first run of test.mjs returned plausible-by-rule for a missense vcla allele via R06 -- exactly the failure mode this module exists to prevent. The scope limit is the fix.

rules.name: Documented adaptation is NOT a documented rescue -- the vegfaa rule
rules.consequence: class stays 'documented' but functional_rescue is set to false/unknown and the verdict MUST NOT be scored as a met requirement
rules.why: This is the rule that stops the COMPENSATORY class quietly rescuing every gap. vegfaa is the clearest case in the field: vegfaa mutants demonstrably upregulate vegfab -- it is one of the founding examples of transcriptional adaptation -- and vegfaa mutants nevertheless have severe, well replicated vascular phenotypes. The adaptation is real and the requirement is still not met. Three states must be kept apart: transcript up, protein up, phenotype rescued. Most of the literature establishes only the first.

sources.quote: Similarly, vegfaa mutants but not morphants show an upregulation of vegfab.

hbegfa, vcla, hif1ab, vegfaa, egfl7 and alcama zebrafish mutants exhibit increased mRNA levels of a paralogue or family member (hereafter referred to as 'adapting gene'), namely hbegfb, vclb, epas1a and epas1b, vegfab, emilin3a and alcamb, respectively (Fig. 1a).

But note the construction: the candidates were overexpressed in MORPHANTS, not mutants, and the authors' own wording is a hedge ('could be compensating'). No direct test that blocking the compensation unmasks a mutant phenotype.

In zebrafish truncating titin (ttn.2) mutants the paralogue Ttn.1 was upregulated 2.55-fold by proteomics, and the phenotype was not rescued: homozygotes were paralysed by 3 dpf with marked cardiac dysfunction and early death. The authors also checked the alternative compensator in the right tissue and found nothing.

decisive_supporting_case.quote2: peptides of Ttn.1 were upregulated throughout (2.55-fold upregulated and 295.6+/-37 Ttn.1 peptides in average compared with 287.8+/-16.8 peptides in WT)
decisive_supporting_case.quote3: although intact, Ttn.1 appears to be insufficient to support viable sarcomere assembly

THE_BIGGEST_HOLE.note: ACROSS THE ENTIRE CORPUS READ FOR THIS RULE BASE, THERE IS NO EXPERIMENT THAT BLOCKS A COMPENSATING GENE'S UPREGULATION IN A MUTANT AND THEREBY UNMASKS A PHENOTYPE. That is the one experiment that would establish functional rescue directly. All pro-rescue evidence is indirect: either a comparison between two DIFFERENT alleles that differ in more than their adaptation status (the RNA-less series also deletes promoter or locus DNA), or rescue of a morphant rather than a mutant. The flagship therapeutic paper measures transcript, pre-mRNA and protein but never tests phenotype rescue at all.
THE_BIGGEST_HOLE.locator: whole paper; all experiments in HEK293T / HAP1 / HeLa / myotubes
THE_BIGGEST_HOLE.consequence: The scoring function must treat 'transcript up' and 'requirement met' as separate, weakly-coupled facts. There is no evidential warrant for collapsing them.

rules.name: Maternal mRNA rescue produces the same signature and is a different mechanism
rules.consequence: unknown, with kind='maternal-confound'. Never 'documented' and never 'plausible-by-rule'.
rules.basis: literature-derived, and explicitly endorsed as a distinction by the journal editors who handled the key paper
rules.why: A zygotic null that still carries wild-type maternal transcript looks exactly like a compensated mutant: silent early, phenotype only later or only in the maternal-zygotic null. This is not compensation, and conflating the two is one of the commonest errors in this literature. It also matters for DELPHI: a designed organism has no maternal contribution from a wild-type mother, so any compensation inferred from a zygotic-only zebrafish null does not transfer to the design at all.

rules.name: Upregulation seen in knockdown too is a protein feedback loop, not transcriptional adaptation
rules.consequence: permits 'documented' with kind='protein-feedback'; this is the ONE mechanism that survives a knockdown-style design gap
rules.basis: literature-derived via review, with named primary cases in other species
rules.why: If the lost protein normally represses its relative, then any loss of the protein -- mutation or knockdown -- de-represses the relative. Concordance between mutant and knockdown is therefore the discriminator between the two mechanisms, and it runs the opposite way to R04.

rules.name: A published outcome for this gene overrides inference
rules.consequence: 'documented', with the case's own direction (compensated or not-rescued) and its sources
rules.why: Where the field has an answer for a gene, the rule base should report that answer rather than re-derive it. The case table carries BOTH directions, because a rule validated only on positives is useless.

counter_evidence.note: A documented case is documented for THAT GENE in THAT ORGANISM at THAT STAGE with THAT ALLELE. It does not generalise to a paralogue, to another tissue, or to a different allele of the same gene -- El-Brolosy's own RNA-less alleles of the very same genes behave oppositely to the decay-competent ones.

rules.name: Absent inputs yield 'unknown', never 'plausible-by-rule'

any.paralogues: undefined/null AND gene not in case table

any.expression: undefined/null when R06 is the only remaining path

rules.basis: design decision of this rule base, stated so it can be audited
rules.why: The failure mode this whole module exists to prevent is hope dressed as a rule. An unknown is the honest output when the evidence needed to apply a rule has not been supplied, and it must be scored as an unmet requirement with a flagged reason, not as a pass.

counter_evidence.note: 'unknown' is NOT evidence that compensation does not occur. It records only that this rule base could not reach a verdict. The distinction between 'unknown' and 'not-expected' is load-bearing and the two must never be collapsed in downstream scoring.

rules.name: No similar, expressed gene means no compensation
rules.why: Both mechanisms need a target: transcriptional adaptation needs a sequence-similar adapting gene, paralogue buffering needs a paralogue. If the caller ASSERTS that there is none, neither mechanism has anything to act through.

sources.quote: Transcriptome analysis in alleles displaying mutant mRNA decay reveals the upregulation of a substantial proportion of the genes that exhibit sequence similarity with the mutated gene's mRNA, suggesting a sequence-dependent mechanism.

counter_evidence.note: Adapting genes need not be paralogues. El-Brolosy's egfl7 adapting genes are emilin family members, and El-Brolosy 2026 explicitly allows non-paralogous adapting genes. So an empty PARALOGUE list does not prove an empty ADAPTING-GENE list, and this rule requires the caller to assert the absence of both. An empty paralogue array that merely reflects our asymmetric Ensembl rows must route to R10 instead.
counter_evidence.quote: It allows the identification of non-paralogous adapting genes, where decay intermediates may hybridize to sense pre-mRNAs at their loci.

rules.name: An organism with no expression data cannot be assessed for compensation
rules.why: The flying fish (Hirundichthys speculiger and relatives) has no expression data in this repo or anywhere we could source. Every expression-dependent rule is therefore inapplicable to the designed organism itself, and compensation verdicts for a flying-fish design rest entirely on zebrafish transfer. That transfer must be visible in the output, not buried.

NUMERIC FOLD-CHANGES / EFFECT SIZES for transcriptional adaptation. There is no quotable fold-change in El-Brolosy 2019's main text or figure legends: every magnitude lives in a qPCR bar panel or a heat map.
